svg.title: Heat pump and reversed Carnot cycle
svg.desc: (a) A heat pump uses work W to take heat Q_c from the cold reservoir at T_c and deliver heat Q_h = Q_c + W to the hot reservoir at T_h. (b) Its ideal cycle is a Carnot cycle run backward: adiabatic expansion A to D, isothermal expansion D to C at T_c (Q_c taken in), adiabatic compression C to B, and isothermal compression B to A at T_h (Q_h given out). An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Illustrative cycle: 300 J transferred from the cold side plus 100 J of work delivers 400 J. Heating
